abstraction_design.rationale: The data abstractions stretch to similar cases well (an Items page reuses cardsFor, Section, CountText, format helpers), but each new detail page re-clones the Switch/Match null-check + Title skeleton, and Card is slowly becoming a grab-bag.

findings.issue: Sprite URL template duplicated between card() (line 113) and homeList's item mapping, so a sprite bug like the Deoxys case must be fixed twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a spriteUrl(id) helper (or build home items through card()) and use it in both places.

findings.issue: The null-check Switch/Match + Title + h1 route skeleton is duplicated verbatim across moves, abilities, types and pokemon detail routes.
findings.suggestion: Extract a DetailPage<T> wrapper (props: resource accessor, render fn) so new sections like Items get the skeleton for free.

findings.issue: Search-param array unwrapping is written twice: first() here and inline in the game() accessor at app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:85-87.
findings.suggestion: Move first() into a shared router-params helper in lib/.

findings.issue: Card carries optional fields (types, hidden) each consumed by a single page, which will grow with every new card variant.
findings.suggestion: Keep Card minimal and pass page-specific extras as children/props to PokemonCards, or accept and document the pattern.

findings.issue: homeList refetches the full species list, all 18 type records and all generations on every query despite the shared cache making them cheap; the query-key fan-out is all in one function.
findings.suggestion: Fine at this scale; if filters grow, split shared lookups into their own query() functions so they cache independently.

summary: A well-layered SolidStart v2 app: file routes are thin, all data work sits behind an explicit query/server boundary, and server internals (API base, caching, dedupe) are confined to one file. Features remove cleanly and changes usually land in pokeapi.ts, though sprite-URL construction and card ordering are each duplicated once. The main extensibility cost is copy-pasted detail-route boilerplate, not bad abstractions.
